bases.guidance: A fine, non-granular earth or mudstone surface without conspicuous sand grains or mandatory lamination. Prefer a neutral, fresh or cut surface; use separate consolidation and fracture settings for clay versus claystone. Search: clay mudstone seamless PBR; fresh claystone texture.

A fine-grained shale surface with a readable bedding or fissility direction. Obtain restrained relief and a directional mask so lamination can follow the geological bedding orientation. Search: laminated shale seamless PBR; shale fresh cut surface.

A subtly granular fine siltstone surface, finer than the sandstone set. Avoid assigning resolvable coarse sand grains simply to make the material visible at a distance. Search: siltstone seamless PBR; fine siltstone texture.

A neutral sand surface with individually separable grains and no dunes, footprints, shells, or cemented bedding baked into the image. Keep grain-scale detail separable from broad color variation. Search: neutral sand grains seamless PBR; sand closeup texture.

A sandstone surface showing packed grains and an intergranular matrix or cement. Prefer an unweathered surface; avoid masonry blocks and strong bedding that cannot be disabled. Search: sandstone fresh surface seamless PBR; sandstone grain matrix texture.

A rounded to subrounded pebble-in-matrix texture with a separate clast mask. Clast scale, abundance, sorting, and matrix texture must be adjustable independently. Search: conglomerate rock seamless PBR; rounded pebble matrix texture.

An angular rock-fragment-in-matrix texture with an independent clast mask and restrained weathering. It must retain angular outlines instead of recoloring the rounded-clast set. Search: breccia rock seamless PBR; angular rock fragments matrix texture.

A fine, relatively uniform carbonate matrix without compulsory fossils, ooids, or large crystals. This supplies the matrix for limestone, argillaceous limestone, and marl recipes. Search: micritic limestone seamless PBR; fine limestone fresh surface.

A restrained interlocking carbonate-crystal surface suitable as a visual starting point for crystalline dolostone. Fine crystal detail should be independent of any large fractures or veins. Search: crystalline dolostone seamless PBR; dolomite rock fresh surface texture.
A pale, very fine and matte chalk surface, with subtle porous relief and no mandatory flint nodules or weathered cliff staining. Search: chalk rock seamless PBR; fresh chalk surface texture.

Recognizable shell fragments in carbonate material, with shell and void masks. Prefer assets that allow shell size and abundance to vary without changing the whole matrix. Search: coquina seamless PBR; shell limestone texture mask.

A carbonate-grain texture with a separate grain-versus-matrix mask. Keep an ooid-specific variant or mask; generic packstone and grainstone must not automatically inherit ooids. Search: granular limestone seamless PBR; oolitic limestone ooid texture.

A carbon-rich rock texture with distinguishable dull and shiny patches, subtle cleat or fracture detail, and a configurable dark palette. A lignite reference can add brown or woody details when warranted. Search: coal seamless PBR; lignite fresh surface texture.

A massive gypsum reference with fine crystalline detail. Fibrous satin spar and transparent crystal specimens are optional variants, not mandatory properties of every gypsum interval. Search: massive gypsum seamless PBR; gypsum rock fresh texture.

A compact massive anhydrite reference with restrained crystalline relief, separate from the gypsum surface. Do not rely on color alone to establish mineral identity. Search: massive anhydrite rock texture; anhydrite fresh core surface.

A rock-salt crystalline surface with adjustable crystal scale. Cube-like crystal cues may be a detail mask, but the bulk interval need not be transparent. This set can be reused visually for sylvite without merging their identities. Search: rock salt halite seamless PBR; halite crystalline texture.

A very fine, dense silica-rich surface with restrained conchoidal-fracture cues. Color, banding, porcelain-like appearance, and sheen should be independent modifiers. Search: chert fresh surface seamless texture; flint conchoidal surface PBR.

An ash-rich pyroclastic matrix with independently maskable lithic, crystal, and glass fragments. Avoid baking a specific welding direction or large lapilli into the only base asset. Search: tuff rock seamless PBR; volcanic ash tuff texture.

A vesicular volcanic material with a usable cavity mask and normal or height map. Visible holes at close range may require geometry instead of surface shading alone. Search: volcanic scoria seamless PBR; cinder vesicular rock texture.

A fine volcanic groundmass suitable for basalt and andesite presets. Use a non-vesicular, non-porphyritic reference as the neutral starting point; add holes or phenocrysts only when justified. Search: basalt fine groundmass seamless PBR; andesite fresh surface texture.

A fine volcanic groundmass for the rhyolite, dacite, and quartz-latite visual presets. Flow banding and conspicuous phenocrysts should be independently selectable rather than compulsory. This shared rendering family is not a claim that all three rocks have identical composition. Search: rhyolite fine groundmass seamless PBR; dacite fresh surface texture.

An interlocking crystal texture with separately adjustable pale feldspar, quartz-like, and dark mineral regions. Use for granite, granodiorite, and quartz monzonite visual presets while retaining separate geological labels. Search: granite interlocking crystals seamless PBR; granodiorite fresh surface texture.
bases.family: Coarse felsic to intermediate intrusive rock

bases.guidance: An interlocking crystal texture with adjustable light-versus-dark mineral regions, suitable for diorite and gabbro visual presets. Do not substitute a rounded sand-grain texture. Search: diorite seamless PBR; gabbro interlocking crystals texture.

A dense volcanic glass surface with conchoidal-fracture detail and configurable smoothness. Keep it dielectric; visible glassy reflection does not make it a metal. Search: obsidian volcanic glass seamless PBR; obsidian fracture texture.

A verified serpentine-rich rock reference with optional mottling and vein masks. Acquire or assign this only if the source label Serpentine denotes a rock; a mineral occurrence does not specify a whole-rock texture. Search: serpentinite fresh surface PBR; serpentine rich rock texture.

Scale grains/crystals independently of beds, fractures, veins, and display exaggeration.
Select loose/consolidated appearance through matrix/contact/fracture cues; no strength simulation.
Add fine clay matrix or pore-filling component using an appropriate mask.
Add subtle fine grains; avoid giant visible silt at physical scale.
Add sand grains to the host; size, composition, and coverage remain independent.
Calcium-carbonate component; mineral, occurrence, brightness, and amount are unspecified.
Explicit calcite component; choose grain/cement/vein occurrence separately.

Directional bedding mask; shaly alone does not require stripes.
Independent planar splitting direction; may intersect bedding.
Rounded clast mask over host matrix; independent size, sorting, and coverage.

Shell-shaped masks; large fragments/cavities may require geometry.

Generic carbonate grains; do not assume shells or ooids.
Disperse grains in a continuous supporting carbonate-mud matrix.
Touching grains; distinguish retained carbonate mud from cement/voids.
Verified binding/baffling/framework fabric; do not assume rigid coral.
Separate palette/finish preset; woody detail only when supported.
Local roughness/smoothness; does not imply metal or transparency.
Directional/warped bands; independent scale and direction.
Rock fragments in matrix; shape/composition/size require separate choices.
Discrete crystal fragments; retain tuff matrix rather than intrusive fabric.
Glass-shard detail in tuff matrix; preserve fragmental appearance.
Flatten/orient suitable pyroclastic patterns; a structural change.
Cavity pattern; use geometry for actual holes/silhouettes.
Change mineral-region palettes/patterns; retain fine/coarse fabric and distinct identity.
Fragmented granitic-derived particles in sediment; preserve clastic fabric.
Broad particle sizes in independently controlled matrix.
Verified soil features on a separately identified parent material.
Metadata only; infer neither wetness nor gloss.
Localized brassy metallic-looking grains/veins; host remains nonmetallic.
Reference-based greenish grains/pellets on a known host.
Fine clay-mineral component; a pale illustrative appearance is optional.
Resolve siderite versus limonite before assigning mineral appearance.
Reference needed for mineral, grain, nodule, coating, or matrix appearance.
Adjust crystal boundaries/detail using reference scale.
Platy dielectric detail; do not imply whole-rock foliation.
Pale platy mica detail with dielectric sheen.
Reference-based dark mica replacement/flecks on host.
Reference-based chlorite replacement; no mandatory global green tint.
Fine pale mica replacement; separate from clay/chalk mixture.
Silica replacement/cement; no mandatory visible veins or gloss increase.
Unspecified carbonate component; mineral and occurrence remain unresolved.
Resolve natural cement versus drilling cement and its composition.
Metadata/status overlay; do not create a new host lithology.
Metadata only until alteration process/mineral appearance is known.
Volcanic ash/fragments within the independently identified sedimentary host.
Resolve mineral occurrence versus rock before selecting a host treatment.
Geometry metadata for a body; does not determine crystal size.
